papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.summary: This protocol describes an integrated chronic preparation for simultaneous two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, EEG, and EMG in freely moving tethered mice, using the retrosplenial cortex as an example target. It yields cellular-resolution calcium signals with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measurements and supports repeated optical access and stimulation-aligned analysis.

papers.title: Sleep EEG distinguishes learned from novel auditory cues without predicting memory retention in a targeted memory reactivation study
papers.summary: Using targeted memory reactivation in 81 healthy young adults, the authors tested whether learned versus novel auditory cues elicit distinct sleep EEG responses and whether encoding or sleep measures predict long-term retention. Learned cues produced stronger delta responses than novel sounds during NREM sleep, but TMR did not improve memory (and was linked to poorer retention of initially weak memories), while pre-sleep memory strength and encoding vividness predicted retention.

papers.title: Experimental Sleep Manipulation and Pain Sensitivity in Healthy Adults: A Focused Review with Emphasis on Sleep Fragmentation.
papers.summary: This focused review narratively synthesized 52 reports (consolidated into 40 publication families, ~1083 participants) on experimental sleep manipulation and pain sensitivity in healthy adults, comparing total sleep deprivation, partial sleep restriction, sleep fragmentation, and awakening paradigms. Total sleep deprivation and partial sleep restriction showed the broadest evidence of hyperalgesia, but an independent effect of sleep fragmentation remains uncertain because direct evidence is limited and awakening protocols also alter sleep duration, architecture, stress, or circadian timing.

papers.title: Revisiting the First Night Effect of Polysomnography Using Wearable EEG Headbands in Older Adults with Sleep Disturbances
papers.summary: Fifty-eight community-dwelling older adults with sleep disturbances completed up to seven nights of wearable EEG headband monitoring including one simultaneous home polysomnography night to characterize the first night effect. Polysomnography nights showed about 35 minutes more wake after sleep onset, 21 minutes less N3 sleep, and 15% lower sleep efficiency, with no differences in total sleep time or REM sleep, suggesting single-night polysomnography may overstate sleep disruption and understate deep sleep.

papers.title: Swimming Toward Recovery: Early Aquatic Therapy as a Bridge to Delayed Environmental Enrichment After Experimental Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: In adult male rats with controlled cortical impact or sham injury, the authors tested whether 7 days of early aquatic therapy could serve as a rehabilitative bridge before delayed environmental enrichment. Sequential aquatic therapy plus enrichment produced greater improvements than enrichment alone on selected motor, spatial learning, and executive outcomes, whereas enrichment alone improved memory retention and anxiety-like behavior, partially supporting the hypothesis.

papers.title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: Combining chromatography and single-molecule fluorescence, the authors show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling in the KaiC hexamer; quantitative modeling indicates that ATP hydrolysis at two monomer-monomer interfaces disassembles hexamers into oligomers that can exchange subunits, and that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling by affecting nucleotide exchange in the CI domain.

papers.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
papers.summary: The authors present EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model that returns typed readouts (choice distributions, proposition probabilities, and ordered-level scores/expectations) from one EEG window with a question and answer specification, trained on one checkpoint and evaluated on held-out splits of 35 public sources. Reported results include 54.08% balanced accuracy on Stieger2021 motor imagery, 70.45% on Sleep-EDF-SC sleep staging, 72.11% per-window accuracy with 0.825 AUROC on CHB-MIT seizure detection, and 1.700 MAE on 0-10 pain ratings, with calibration lowering negative log-likelihood and direct readout cutting batch-1 latency 1.94-fold.

papers.title: Adult EEG Reactivity in Rat Offspring After an Uncomplicated Birth Is Not Significantly Altered by Gestational Antibiotics.
papers.summary: In adult Wistar rat offspring born without perinatal asphyxia, gestational exposure to antibiotics, probiotics, or their combination produced no significant differences in EEG burst-count reactivity or burst-suppression reactivity index during intermittent photic stimulation. The authors conclude that gestational antibiotics may impair resilience to perinatal asphyxia without a readily detectable long-term effect after uncomplicated birth.

papers.title: Large-Scale Neural Slowing Measured with Electroencephalography Indexes Secondary Thalamic Degeneration in Stroke.
papers.summary: Using resting-state EEG parameterization and corticothalamic circuit modeling alongside structural MRI in 25 stroke patients, this study found widespread spectral abnormalities (increased aperiodic exponent and offset, lower alpha frequency, reduced beta power) and inferred broad thalamic disinhibition. These abnormalities were strongly associated with ipsilesional thalamic atrophy despite absent direct thalamic damage, supporting large-scale neural slowing as a clinically feasible biomarker of secondary thalamic degeneration.

papers.title: The Orexinergic System in Alzheimer's Disease: From Sleep Disruption to Accelerated Neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the bidirectional relationship between sleep-wake dysregulation and Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology, emphasizing the orexinergic system as a mechanistic link between hyperarousal, impaired sleep consolidation, and altered amyloid dynamics. It reports that high CSF orexin-A levels occur in mild cognitive impairment and AD dementia, but that robust proof of disease-modifying effects from sleep-targeting or orexin-modulating interventions remains limited.

papers.title: Effect of Intraindividual Variability in Sleep on Long-Term Memory Encoding in Sleep-Restricted Individuals.
papers.summary: In a sleep-restriction study with 44 participants, a variable short sleep schedule (8-4-8-4-6 h time-in-bed) led to poorer declarative memory encoding than a control schedule, evidenced by more 'unsure' responses at retrieval, whereas a stable short sleep schedule did not impair memory and increased correct rejections.

papers.title: Monitoring Reduced Vigilance Using an Eyeglass-Type EEG System.
papers.summary: Using a custom eyeglass-type EEG device across a two-phase experiment with 21 participants, this study identified the low-alpha to high-beta power ratio as a mental-fatigue-sensitive index and combined it with a theta-plus-alpha drowsiness index from temporal channels via an OR rule. In pseudo-real-time evaluation of 16 participants, the fusion model achieved mean accuracy of 70.31% with 10.40% false positives, providing preliminary evidence for wearable reduced-vigilance monitoring.

papers.title: Mitigating Sleep Inertia and Maintaining Neurobehavioral Performance in Shift Workers via Multisensory (Music and Light) Intervention: A Preliminary Field Study.
papers.summary: In a preliminary field crossover study of 17 railway shift workers, a wearable dual-phase multisensory device (sleep-promoting music in darkness before sleep; uplifting music with blue light on awakening) maintained PVT response speed, reduced end-of-shift lapses, and was associated with longer sleep duration, though overall sleepiness was not significantly reduced. A separate EEG study in 10 adults showed increased slow-to-fast power ratio during sleep-onset stimulation and transiently lower theta power early in wake-up stimulation.

papers.title: Peripheral sensory clocks drive nitroglycerin-induced rhythmic pain sensitivity.
papers.journal: The journal of headache and pain
papers.summary: Using tissue-specific Bmal1 knockout mice in a nitroglycerin-induced headache model, the authors show that loss of Bmal1 in trigeminal and dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons abolishes the diurnal rhythm of pain sensitivity without affecting basal nociception or hypersensitivity, whereas suprachiasmatic nucleus-specific deletion eliminates locomotor rhythms but not pain rhythms.

papers.title: The EEG-Respiratory Gap: a deep learning biomarker associated with long-term mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
papers.summary: The authors developed a deep-learning model (AHIbrain) to estimate the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel and derived EEG-Respiratory Gap metrics (ΔAHIbrain and AHIbrain,event-free) that were associated with all-cause, non-cardiovascular, and cardiovascular mortality beyond AHI in participants free of cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Mapping global glymphatic system research (2012-2025): a scientometric and knowledge-mapping review integrating bioinformatics perspectives on aging.
papers.summary: This scientometric and knowledge-mapping review analyzed glymphatic system research from 2012 to 2025, identifying a shift from animal to human studies and five thematic clusters, and integrated GEO dataset analysis showing aging- and glymphatic-related genes converging on PI3K-Akt and FoxO signaling.

papers.title: Lactobacillus Fermentation-Derived γ-Aminobutyric Acid Improves Sleep Parameters in Invertebrate and Vertebrate Models.
papers.summary: Lactobacillus fermentation-derived gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABArelax®) increased total sleep time and reduced locomotor activity in Drosophila, increased GABAergic and serotonergic receptor expression and brain GABA/5-HT in mice, and reduced wakefulness while prolonging non-REM sleep and enhancing delta-wave activity in rats.

papers.title: Beyond dream enactment: Pharmacological effects on REM atonia in REM sleep behavior disorder - a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 17 reports found that current evidence does not establish consistent pharmacological improvement in quantitative REM sleep without atonia in REM sleep behavior disorder, despite frequently reported symptomatic benefits, and highlights small samples and methodological heterogeneity as limitations.

papers.title: Integrating bioethnography into sleep research: generating better measures, hypotheses, and interpretations.
papers.summary: This report presents bioethnography—integrating sustained ethnographic engagement with epidemiological research—as a complementary approach to sleep research, demonstrating through a study of midlife women in a Mexico City cohort how open-ended inquiry reshapes hypotheses, reveals unmeasured social processes, and refines interpretation of quantitative sleep metrics. The authors argue this yields more valid, interpretable 'better numbers' while outlining practical integration strategies and limitations.

papers.title: Single- and Multi-SNP Genotype Analyses of the Circadian-Related SLC20A2 Gene Reveal Sex-Specific Associations with Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD).
papers.summary: Testing five SLC20A2 SNPs and multi-SNP genotypes in a phenotyped undergraduate population, the study found three SNPs (rs6988483, rs13281070, rs3763510) associated with self-reported SAD severity, with effects concentrated in males, and identified eight multi-SNP combinations; one risk genotype conferred roughly ninefold greater odds of SAD in females without corresponding association with general depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Diurnal Variation in Human Breast Milk: Multi-Omic Characterization and Implications for Infant Circadian Development.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 89 mother-infant dyads plus paired noon/midnight breast milk samples from 20 lactating women, the authors characterized diurnal multi-omic variation in milk. They identified 20 bacterial genera differing by sampling time and reported midnight enrichment of specific taxa and lipid/amino acid metabolism pathways, suggesting potential implications for infant circadian development.

papers.title: Shared sleep fragmentation in undergraduate roommates: dyadic actigraphy in a dense urban campus setting.
papers.summary: Using four nights of wrist actigraphy in 29 undergraduate roommate dyads versus pseudo-dyads, the study found roommate concordance clearest for awakening frequency (ICC = 0.38) and correlated night-to-night WASO deviations (r = 0.29) that persisted after calendar-timing adjustment, indicating modest shared sleep fragmentation beyond romantic partners.

papers.title: Impact of Ambient Temperature on PAP Adherence: A Retrospective Analysis of a Prospective OSA Cohort.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 342 OSA patients initiating auto-adjusting PAP, higher ambient temperature at initiation was associated with lower early adherence (OR 0.95 per 1°C; adherence 61.7% for May–September vs 75.1% for October–April), with temperature contributing to model discrimination comparably to baseline AHI.

papers.title: Impaired corneal nerve repair and regeneration after injury in mouse sleep deprivation model.
papers.summary: In a mouse corneal injury model, sleep deprivation reduced corneal central and peripheral nerve fiber density and sensitivity on day 6 post-injury, lowered corneal NGF expression, and transcriptomic analysis showed downregulation of nerve-related gene expression and inhibition of nerve repair pathways.

papers.title: Sea-Level Polysomnography and Periodic Breathing During Acute Normobaric Hypoxia in Healthy Adults: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: In this exploratory study, 54 healthy adults underwent sea-level polysomnography and repeat polysomnography under acute normobaric hypoxia simulating ~3500 m; 11 participants developed sleep-disordered breathing with periodic breathing. Sea-level oxygen desaturation index was independently associated with hypoxic periodic breathing (AUC 0.798; cutoff 1.15 events/h: sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 79.1%).

papers.title: Plasma Metabolic Proteomics Links Phenoconversion and Disease-Specific Brain 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Pattern Expressions in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 116 patients across the RBD-LBD continuum, plasma metabolic proteomics identified 16 differentially expressed proteins enriched in neutrophil degranulation pathways, with NT-proBNP uniquely upregulated in isolated RBD and associated with earlier phenoconversion. Elevated NT-proBNP correlated with orthostatic intolerance and increased PD- and DLB-related metabolic brain pattern expressions.

papers.title: Neuroinflammation in central vestibular compensation and in the pathogenesis of vestibular disorders: preclinical evidence, mechanistic bridges, and a causal research agenda.
papers.summary: This evidence-graded review synthesizes preclinical evidence that neuroinflammation modulates central vestibular compensation, proposing a dual-phase, state-dependent glial hypothesis and a causal research agenda. Direct evidence is limited to 20 original preclinical studies, and neuroinflammation is currently considered a candidate modulator requiring causal validation.

papers.title: Condition-associated EEG signatures in N-back tasks: temporal dynamics, classification, and generalization.
papers.summary: Investigated EEG signatures of mental workload in 15 adults during two N-back paradigms using an 8-channel setup, finding modest and context-dependent classification performance with distinct spectral and ERP patterns for N-level versus speed manipulations, and limited cross-paradigm generalization.

papers.title: AI-assisted development of a rule-based pipeline for pre-examination screening in clinical neuropsychology: An exploratory method-development study.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society : JINS
papers.summary: An exploratory method-development study presents a rule-based pre-examination screening pipeline for clinical neuropsychology, developed with a large language model as coding assistant but deployed deterministically. Applied to retrospective data from 105 adults (65 IBS, 40 controls), the tool flagged multi-domain findings in 60% and demonstrated transparent, clinician-gated reports requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: Natural Antioxidants in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Future Perspectives.
papers.summary: Reviewed evidence on natural antioxidant compounds and plant extracts as protective interventions against sleep deprivation-induced oxidative stress and inflammation, highlighting their pleiotropic mechanisms but calling for further mechanistic and clinical studies.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Insights to Rational Interventions in Parkinson's Disease: An Integrated Approach with a Patient Perspective.
papers.summary: A single early-stage Parkinson's disease patient was observed over two years during five overlapping interventions targeting disease-relevant pathways, with clinical stability but reduced striatal DAT binding at follow-up. Wearable monitoring suggested reduced slow-wave sleep that increased after a structured bedtime routine, illustrating the discordance between clinical stability and underlying disease progression.

papers.title: PFedHASNet: A Personalized Federated Hybrid Analog-Spike Network for Multi-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
papers.summary: PFedHASNet is a personalized federated hybrid analog-spike network for multi-subject motor imagery EEG decoding that integrates continuous-valued features, LIF spike responses, and channel-wise log-variance statistics in a shared encoder with client-private residual adapters. Across four public MI-EEG datasets, it achieved the highest mean client macro-F1 among 18 model configurations while maintaining a compact client-side model.

papers.title: Integrating Inflammation, Pathway Modulation, and Circadian Clock Genes: Conventional and Phytochemical Strategies for Safer Osteoporosis Therapy.
papers.summary: This review discusses integrating circadian biology with conventional and phytochemical therapies for osteoporosis, highlighting that time-sensitive administration aligned with circadian rhythms may improve efficacy and reduce side effects. It reports that phytochemicals such as resveratrol, icariin, genistein, quercetin, and baicalein show osteoprotective effects via antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and modulation of RANKL/OPG, AMPK/SIRT1, ESR, NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin pathways.

papers.title: Multi-scale feature fusion and neural architecture search for electroencephalography-based affective-state recognition in public benchmark datasets.
papers.summary: The study evaluated MFANet, a framework combining parallel multi-scale 1D convolutional branches, channel-wise attention, and neural architecture search-guided LSTM temporal modeling, for binary EEG affective-state classification on DEAP and DREAMER. Using trial-grouped subject-dependent cross-validation, the full model achieved mean accuracies of about 97.2% for valence, 97.3% for arousal, and 97.1% for dominance on DEAP, exceeding a DGCNN baseline by roughly 3.4-4.1 percentage points.

papers.title: Footwear-Related Modulation of Scalp EEG Theta/Alpha Ratio During Walking in Children: An Exploratory Within-Subject Study.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
papers.summary: In a within-subject randomized comparison of 37 typically developing children aged 6-7 years walking under barefoot, barefoot-style footwear, and conventional structured footwear conditions, mobile scalp EEG showed that conventional structured footwear produced significantly higher global Theta/Alpha ratios than both other conditions (F(2,72)=14.57, p<0.001), while barefoot and barefoot-style conditions did not differ. No significant differences emerged in absolute theta, alpha, or beta power, Beta/Alpha ratio, or Shannon entropy.

papers.title: Process, Heterogeneity, and Modifiable Risk Factors of Postoperative Recovery After Cardiac Surgery.
papers.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
papers.summary: In a multicenter prospective cohort of 2,993 patients undergoing nonemergent cardiac surgery assessed with the Fuwai-Cardiac Recovery Scale at baseline and 8 postoperative timepoints, group-based trajectory modeling identified three distinct poor recovery patterns across symptoms and functional items, and the proportion achieving a total score ≤30 rose from 77.4% at discharge to 97.7% at month 3. Modifiable risk factors associated with poor recovery patterns included smoking (shortness of breath, OR 1.55), obesity (poor mobility, OR 1.52), and anemia (poor appetite, OR 1.47; fatigue, OR 1.36).

papers.title: Cognitive Performance in Experienced Dancers: A Virtual Reality Comparative Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of dance medicine & science : official publication of the International Association for Dance Medicine & Science
authors: Luciane Aparecida Pascucci Sande de Souza
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared 13 experienced dancers and 13 non-dancers on reaction time, decision time, attention, and inhibitory control using the immersive NeuroSport Arena VR system with simple reaction time and Go/No-Go tasks. No significant between-group differences were found, but dancers showed significantly lower reaction time variability (F=5.63, P=.026) and a non-significant trend toward faster responses (256.30 vs 280.15 ms, P=.091).

papers.title: Acute Encephalopathy in a Patient with Dravet Syndrome Successfully Managed with Therapeutic Normothermia and Vitamin Supplementation Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 3-year-4-month-old girl with Dravet syndrome who developed acute encephalopathy after febrile convulsive status epilepticus during RSV infection and was treated with intensive care, continuous midazolam, 48-hour targeted temperature management, and vitamin supplementation (thiamine, pyridoxine, L-carnitine). Despite acute-phase diffuse cerebral atrophy, she recovered to her prior developmental status within 4 months, with subsequent improvement in cerebral atrophy on follow-up MRI.

papers.title: Pathological mechanisms of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline.
papers.summary: This review constructs a mechanistic network of 'lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine' crosstalk linking unhealthy lifestyle stressors to chronic low-grade inflammation, ectopic fat deposition, and skeletal muscle decline. It proposes that immunometabolic reprogramming and neuroendocrine axis decline act as core drivers amplifying tissue microenvironment remodeling and body composition imbalance.

papers.title: Solutions to Reduce Burnout Syndrome Among Perioperative Healthcare Providers in Low-Resource Settings: A Qualitative Study.
papers.summary: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 61 perioperative care providers across public hospitals in Rwanda to identify solutions to burnout within a multilevel model. Participants reported strategies spanning individual coping and basic needs, interpersonal support networks, hospital organization and workload, systemic staffing and financing, and cultural factors such as recognition and respect, indicating that effective burnout solutions must be adapted to context and implemented across all levels.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
